title: 25 tests guard the promises: nothing private leaks, nothing sold comes back, everything restores
summary: The automated suite now checks every public file for seeded private values, replays a week-later spreadsheet, restores exports into fresh installs, rejects a tampered backup, and times a 1,500-work catalog. All 25 tests pass. A scripted browser run also went from an empty install to a restored copy without errors.
why: Portability and privacy are only selling points if they keep being true after every change. These tests are the receipts behind the claims ledger.
detail: Found and fixed along the way: multi-line notes and provenance lost their line breaks on import; merging a duplicate row could silently change a work's inventory number (it now keeps the catalog's number and records the other one); a delayed refresh on the import page could replace whatever page you had moved to; one page had duplicate form ids. On an Apple M4 Mac mini, previewing and applying 1,500 rows took about 0.6 seconds and searching took 2 to 3 ms. A workspace made by the first engine version opened in the current version with its colours and custom CSS intact. Still unverified: real gallery files, a real owner, screen readers, Windows, and the generated Artsy file inside a real Artsy account.
next: Test the one-prompt install as an assistant would follow it, then make the code public once Paul approves the repository.
author: Claude
